evidence:
RE-CHECKED ON 18 SEPTEMBER 2026, build v26.36.7-29ca209, after the developer added the line on each row that says how it matched, and asked whether this is still relevant.

WHAT CHANGED: each near-spelling row now carries a visible marker reading 'close match', so a person can see why it is there.

WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: the list itself. Typing 'Marlene' returns eighteen results across five groups, exactly as reported. Sixteen of the eighteen do not contain the word typed - Darlene in five places, Charlene in two street addresses, Martens as a company name, four MARINE battery parts, a vehicle owned by Martens, a supplier called Coeur d'Alene and a purchase order carrying one of the marine parts. The near-spellings are the same five words as before and they score the same to three decimal places, so the matching itself has not been touched.

THE PRODUCT IS BEHAVING AS THE REQUIREMENT IS WRITTEN. The requirement accepts a near-spelling when it is at least 70 per cent similar, and on a seven-letter word that permits two letters to differ - which is exactly what these five words are. This check exists because the older version could not return them at all, so it is a difference between the two versions for the Product Owner to rule on, not a coding mistake.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL PICTURE, in fairness: the customer actually being looked for now sits second of eighteen, not buried.
